summary.tagline: Horn Head (Irish: Corrán Binne, meaning 'point of the cliff') is a peninsula in northwest County Donegal, Irel

days.title: Coastal Heights and Viewpoints
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Cliffs von Horn Head
stops.detail: On the side of the peninsula facing the Atlantic, the cliffs of Horn Head rise almost vertically from the sea to a height of up to 180 m and represent an internationally important colony for breeding seabirds, including shags and razorbills.

stops.name: Beobachtungstürme
stops.detail: On Horn Head, there are remains of two observation towers, one from the time of the Napoleonic Wars, the other from the Second World War.

stops.name: Tory Island
stops.detail: From both you have a view of the Atlantic and Tory Island.

days.title: Ancient History and Blowholes
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Portal Tomb von Claggan
stops.detail: Horn Head is home to numerous remains of Neolithic stone circles, court tombs and portal tombs (Claggan Portal Tomb, Muntermellan Portal Tomb) along with prehistoric field markings.

stops.name: McSwyne’s gun
stops.detail: With McSwyne's gun, there is a blowhole on the west side of Horn Head through which, during storms, the water is driven up to 90 m high with extreme noise development.
